These statements involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties and other factors that may cause our actual results, levels of activity, performance or achievements to be materially different from any future results, levels of activity, performance, or achievements expressed or implied by forward-looking statements.

Forward-looking statements can be identified by words such as “may,” “expects,” “plans,” “anticipates,” “believes,” “estimates,” “intends” or “continue.” Actual results may differ materially because of factors the Company cannot predict or control, including the outcome of the proceedings described in this report and the implementation of the Court’s Order of August 11, 2026. The Company undertakes no obligation to update forward-looking statements except as required by law.

Explanatory Note

This Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q is filed after its due date, on behalf of the Company by Jacob Sherman, appointed successor custodian by the Eighth Judicial District Court of Clark County, Nevada (the “Court”) on October 6, 2026 and authorized by its order of October 12, 2026 to act as principal executive officer and principal financial officer for the Company’s Exchange Act reports. The Company has no directors or officers. The custodian held no position with the Company during the period covered by this report and has relied on the records delivered to him.

On August 11, 2026 the Court entered an order (the “Order”, Exhibit 99.1) that removed the former custodian, declared void a series of transactions between the Company and entities he controlled, cancelled the related shares, rescinded the 1-for-1,200 reverse stock split of January 20, 2026 and allowed a creditor claim. The Company’s previously issued financial statements for 2019 through the quarter ended March 31, 2026 should no longer be relied upon; the comparative periods in this report are restated (Note 2).

NOTES TO THE UNAUDITED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

For the Six Months Ended June 30, 2026

1. GENERAL ORGANIZATION AND BUSINESS

GlobalTek Ventures, Inc. (formerly Ameritek Ventures, Inc.; “GlobalTek” or the “Company”) is a Nevada corporation organized in 2010. Its name was changed on April 16, 2026 by its then custodian; the Order described in Note 2 directs that no charter documents be amended pending the appointment of a neutral, and the validity of the name change and of the 2025 increase in authorized common stock has not been determined. The common stock is quoted on the OTC Markets under the symbol ATVK.

The Company’s only revenue-producing activity is the rental of furnished condominiums in Chicago, Illinois through Chicago Real Estate Partners, LLC, begun in the third quarter of 2025. Its former software business (Ecker Capital, LLC) was sold in October 2024 and Galaxy Batteries, Inc. was purchased in August 2025; both transactions were declared void by the Order (Note 6). Its other subsidiaries (AeroPass, Augumum, CordTell, Equock and WeeBeeO, Inc. of Indiana and DittoMask, Inc. of Wyoming) have no operations. Ecker Capital, LLC is not consolidated because its membership interests have not been returned to the Company.

The Company has had no directors or officers since August 11, 2026. Jacob Sherman, appointed successor custodian on October 6, 2026, is authorized by the Court to act as principal executive and principal financial officer for the Company’s Exchange Act reports (Note 16); he held no position with the Company during the periods presented and prepared these financial statements from the records delivered to him.

Going concern

The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared assuming that the Company will continue as a going concern. As of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash of $29,328, current liabilities of $2,192,354, current assets of $30,815, a working capital deficit of $2,161,539 and a stockholders’ deficit of $1,157,138. The Company generated operating revenue of $11,706, incurred a net loss of $732,925 and used $101,217 of cash in operating activities during the six months ended June 30, 2026, and has relied on related-party financing and other external sources of liquidity to fund operations. Current liabilities include $576,706 due to Meridian Pacific Holdings, LLC, which the Court has allowed and on which interest continues to accrue, and $1,573,294 of advances from affiliates of the former custodian, which cannot be expected to continue. The Company has no directors or officers and its affairs are subject to the supervision of the Court. These conditions raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date these consolidated financial statements are issued.

2. COURT ORDER AND RESTATEMENT OF PREVIOUSLY ISSUED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

Background

Shaun Passley, PhD was appointed custodian of the Company by the Eighth Judicial District Court, Clark County, Nevada (the “Court”) on November 9, 2020 under NRS 78.347 and acted as custodian and sole director and officer until August 11, 2026. On August 11, 2026, after trial of the derivative claims of two creditors and the Company’s claims against them, the Court entered Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Order in Case No. A-20-822695-B (the “Order”, filed as Exhibit 99.1).

The Court (i) removed Dr. Passley as custodian, held that he had not been validly appointed as a director or officer (ii) declared void ab initio transactions including the Management Services Agreement with Epazz, Inc., the mergers of Bozki, Inc. and VW Win Century, Inc., the Technology Exclusive License Agreement with ZenaTech, Inc., the Stock Compensation Agreement, the sale of Ecker Capital, LLC, the purchase of Galaxy Batteries, Inc., cancelled the shares issued under them and left the debt assumed under them with the originating party; (iii) rescinded the 1-for-1,200 reverse stock split of January 20, 2026; (iv) allowed the creditor claim of Meridian Pacific Holdings, LLC (“Meridian”) at $579,100 as of August 11, 2026 with interest accruing. The Company has applied the Order as written; Dr. Passley’s challenges to it are described in Note 14.

Epazz, Inc. notes assumed in the mergers (principal $1,014,094; accrued interest $699,009 at December 31, 2025) and related interest derecognized; 50,000,000 conversion shares cancelled; commitment-fee amortization reversed.

Recognized with accrued interest and late charge (Note 10).

Shares issued for Galaxy Batteries (10,000,000,000) and the $37,000,000 common control adjustment account reversed; 366,000,000 shares issued in January 2025 under the voided compensation and management agreements cancelled and 2025 stock-based compensation of $477,722 ($183,000 in the 2025 periods presented) reversed; other shares issued to Dr. Passley and his affiliates and the Series B, C and D preferred stock cancelled (Note 11); reverse stock split rescinded. No effect on total equity.

R6 – Management fees

Fees of $479,565 billed by Epazz, Inc. under the voided Management Services Agreement and unpaid at December 31, 2025 derecognized from the beginning of the earliest period presented (Note 12).

The Order has not yet been implemented on the transfer agent’s register, which continues to show 9,222,729 post-split common shares and the preferred stock as previously reported; the cancelled shares have not been surrendered and the ZenaTech shares and Ecker membership interests have not been exchanged. 3. SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING PRINCIPLES

Basis of Preparation

The consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes are prepared under the accrual basis of accounting in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles of the United States of America (“US GAAP”) for interim financial information and Article 8 of Regulation S-X. They do not include all of the information and notes required by US GAAP for complete financial statements. In the opinion of the successor custodian, the financial statements include all adjustments, consisting of normal recurring adjustments and the restatement adjustments described in Note 2, considered necessary for a fair presentation of the Company’s financial position, results of operations, stockholders’ equity (deficit) and cash flows for the periods presented. The results for interim periods are not necessarily indicative of results for the full year. The December 31, 2025 consolidated balance sheet is derived from the previously audited balance sheet as restated; the restated amounts have not been audited. The previously issued annual financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025 should no longer be relied upon (Note 2).

Principles of consolidation

The consolidated financial statements include the Company and its wholly owned subsidiaries (Note 1); intercompany balances and transactions are eliminated.

Use of Estimates

Preparation of financial statements under U.S. GAAP requires estimates and assumptions that affect reported amounts. Significant judgements include the application of the Order where it does not resolve a matter (Notes 2 and 11), the carrying amount of advances from affiliates (Note 12), useful lives, impairment, contingencies (Note 14) and the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets (Note 15). Actual results could differ.

Cash and Cash Equivalents

Cash and cash equivalents comprise bank balances and highly liquid instruments with original maturities of three months or less.

Property and Equipment

Property and equipment, including real estate held for rental, is stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment and depreciated on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives (real estate 27.5 years; furniture 5 years; computers and equipment 3–5 years; website development 3 years; land not depreciated). Repairs and maintenance are expensed. Long-lived assets, including franchise and development rights (amortized over 10 years), are reviewed for impairment when events indicate that the carrying amount may not be recoverable; an impairment is recognized when the carrying amount exceeds the undiscounted cash flows and is measured at the excess over fair value. The FlexFridge patent, product development costs and goodwill were fully impaired in 2025.

Share-based payments to employees and non-employees are measured at the grant-date fair value of the equity instruments or, if more reliably measurable, of the goods or services received, and recognized as the services are received. No stock-based compensation was recognized in the periods presented as restated (Note 2); the 91,244 post-split shares issued to Maxim Group Partners, LLC on May 19, 2026 for investment banking services were measured at the quoted market price, $620,459, and expensed.

Basic and Diluted Net Earnings per Share

Basic earnings (loss) per share is net income (loss) divided by the weighted-average common shares outstanding; diluted earnings (loss) per share also includes dilutive potential common shares, which are excluded when anti-dilutive (Note 13).

Revenue Recognition

Rental income from furnished condominium units is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term under ASC 842; tenant security deposits are recorded as liabilities. The Company had no revenue within the scope of ASC 606 and no accounts receivable in the periods presented.

Investment in Securities

Equity securities with readily determinable fair values are measured at fair value through earnings (ASC 321). The ZenaTech, Inc. shares received under the voided sale of Ecker Capital, LLC are not recognized because the Company has no rights to them under the Order (Note 2).

Income Taxes

Income taxes are accounted for under the asset-and-liability method (ASC 740); deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when realization is not more likely than not (Note 15).

Segment Information

The Company has one operating and reportable segment, the rental of residential real estate; the chief operating decision maker (the former sole director and, since October 6, 2026, the custodian) reviews financial information on a consolidated basis.

Recent Accounting Pronouncements

No recently issued accounting pronouncements are expected to have a material effect on the consolidated financial statements.

The following discussion should be read with the unaudited consolidated financial statements and notes in Item 1, in particular Notes 2 and 11, and the forward-looking statements note above. It has been prepared by the successor custodian, who held no position with the Company during the periods discussed.

Business Overview

GlobalTek Ventures, Inc. (formerly Ameritek Ventures, Inc.) is a Nevada corporation. Its only operating activity is the rental of furnished condominiums in Chicago through Chicago Real Estate Partners, LLC, which bought its first units in the third quarter of 2025 and two further units in 2026. Its former software business was sold in October 2024 and Galaxy Batteries, Inc. was acquired in August 2025; the Order declared these and the other related-party agreements described in Note 2 void, the ZenaTech shares that represented most of the previously reported assets are no longer recognized, and the strategic plans that depended on affiliates of the former custodian are no longer pursued. The successor custodian’s mandate is to complete the Company’s rehabilitation, nominate an independent board and then end the custodianship.

Restatement

The December 31, 2025 balance sheet and the 2025 comparative periods are restated for the Order (Note 2). Stockholders’ equity at December 31, 2025 changed from $7,800,321 as previously reported to a deficit of $1,044,672, principally from the derecognition of the ZenaTech shares ($10,471,466), partly offset by the derecognition of the Epazz, Inc. notes, accrued interest and management fees ($2,192,668) and the recognition of the Meridian liability ($566,195). The net loss for the six months ended June 30, 2025 changed from $7,526,738 to $4,644, mainly from the reversal of the loss on the ZenaTech shares and of stock-based compensation under the voided agreements.

Going concern

The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared assuming that the Company will continue as a going concern. As of June 30, 2026, the Company had cash of $29,328, current liabilities of $2,192,354, current assets of $30,815, a working capital deficit of $2,161,539 and a stockholders’ deficit of $1,157,138. The Company generated operating revenue of $11,706 during the six months ended June 30, 2026 and has relied on related-party financing and other external sources of liquidity to fund operations. These conditions raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date these consolidated financial statements are issued.

The Company evaluates the carrying value of goodwill each year and between annual evaluations if events occur or circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of the reporting unit below its carrying amount. Such circumstances could include, but are not limited to (1) a significant adverse change in legal factors or in business climate, (2) unanticipated competition, or (3) an adverse action or assessment by a regulator. When evaluating whether goodwill is impaired, the Company compares the fair value of the reporting unit to which the goodwill is assigned to the reporting unit’s carrying amount, including goodwill. The fair value of the reporting unit is estimated using a combination of the income, or discounted cash flows, approach, and the market approach, which utilizes comparable companies’ data. If the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds its fair value, then the amount of the impairment loss must be measured.

The impairment loss would be calculated by comparing the implied fair value of reporting unit goodwill to its carrying amount. In calculating the implied fair value of reporting unit goodwill, the fair value of the reporting unit is allocated to all of the other assets and liabilities of that unit based on their fair values. The excess of the fair value of a reporting unit over the amount assigned to its other assets and liabilities is the implied fair value of goodwill. An impairment loss would be recognized when the carrying amount of goodwill exceeds its implied fair value. Under FASB ASC 820-10-5, fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date (an exit price). The standard outlines a valuation framework and creates a fair value hierarchy in order to increase the consistency and comparability of fair value measurements and the related disclosures. Under GAAP, certain assets and liabilities must be measured at fair value, and FASB ASC 820-10-50 details the disclosures that are required for items measured at fair value.

The Company’s financial assets and liabilities are measured using inputs from the three levels of the fair value hierarchy. The three levels are as follows:

Level 1 – Inputs are unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the Company has the ability to access at the measurement date.

Level 2 – Inputs include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are not active, inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability (e.g., interest rates, yield curves, etc.), and inputs that are derived principally from or corroborated by observable market data by correlation or other means (market corroborated inputs).

Level 3 – Unobservable inputs that reflect our assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability.

The Company accounts for income taxes in accordance with ASC 740, Income Taxes, using the asset and liability method. Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on temporary differences between the financial statement carrying amounts and the tax bases of assets and liabilities and are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply in the periods in which those temporary differences are expected to reverse. The Company recognizes the benefit of uncertain tax positions only when such positions are more likely than not to be sustained upon examination by the relevant taxing authorities. Interest and penalties related to uncertain tax positions, if any, are recognized as a component of income tax expense.

Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures

We have performed an evaluation under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our President, and our Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO), of the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures, (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Exchange Act) as of December 31, 2025. Based on that evaluation, our management, including our President, and CEO and CFO, concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of December 31, 2025 to provide reasonable assurance that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports filed or submitted by us under the Exchange Act is (i) recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC’s rules and forms and (ii) accumulated and communicated to our management, including our principal executive officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure due to the material weaknesses described below.

Based on our evaluation under the framework described above, our management concluded that we had “material weaknesses” (as such term is defined below) in our control environment and financial reporting process consisting of the following as of the Evaluation Date:

1) | lack of a functioning audit committee for the entire fiscal year resulting in ineffective oversight in the establishment and monitoring of required internal control and procedures; and

2) | inadequate segregation of duties consistent with control objectives.

A “material weakness” is defined under SEC rules as a deficiency, or a combination of deficiencies, in internal control over financial reporting such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of a company’s annual or interim financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis by the company’s internal controls.

A system of controls, no matter how well designed and operated, cannot provide absolute assurance that the objectives of the system of controls are met, and no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, within a company have been detected.
